v.why: With edge 0 empty, node 1 gets no input, so a conv reconnects the entire 0->1 branch.
Reactivating the 0->2 edge with a strong conv creates a new feature path, which helps more than a swap.
Adding a conv to an empty 1->2 edge creates a deeper path, which helps more than swapping ops.
Filling an empty direct input-output edge with a strong conv adds a whole new path, whereas replacing an existing op yields less gain.
A conv on an empty 1->3 edge creates a new path from node 1 to the output.
A conv on an empty 2->3 edge connects node 2 to the output, which adds a path.
If edge 0 is none, node 1 has no input, so edge 2 carries nothing and editing it matters little.
If node 1 has no input, edge 4 carries nothing, so the conv upgrade is wasted.
With 2->3 removed, edge 2's output is a dead end, so a stronger op there brings nothing.
Adding a skip connection where the direct edge was absent restores a gradient-friendly path, a bigger gain than swapping one existing op.

Edge 5 being `none` cuts node 2 off from the output, so edge 2 has no downstream path. I dropped the hypotheses that depend on redundancy between edges or on competing effects.
